Silver prices could be headed back to $50 - Bloomberg's McGlone
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Silver prices could remain under pressure for years as the precious metal struggles to recover from its historic rally, and one market strategist warns that prices could fall back to $50 an ounce in the near term before finding meaningful support. In a recent note, Mike McGlone, senior commodity strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence, said that silver faces a difficult technical outlook, with prices potentially remaining trapped between $50 and $84 an ounce for years. The bearish outlook comes as spot silver currently trades at $59.11 an ounce, down nearly 2% on the day.

‘Single-asset portfolio': Kazakhstan plans gold sales as holdings reach 78% of reserves
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) –Kazakhstan's central bank has announced plans to rebalance its reserves by selling off some of its massive gold reserves, flipping one of the world’s leading buyers into a big seller for the remainder of 2026. Aliya Moldabekova, Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Kazakhstan, explained in a recent interview that the current multi-decade highs in Treasury yields make dollar assets very attractive. “We haven’t seen levels like this in a long time,” Moldabekova said. “This makes the dollar an attractive option, thereby reducing the appeal of gold as an investment asset.”

Gold price holding steady as U.S. existing home sales rise 1.5%
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market continues to hold its own, trading in relatively neutral territory even as positive U.S. housing market data reduces safe-haven demand for the precious metal. Total existing-home sales, including single-family homes, townhomes, condominiums and co-ops, increased 1.5% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.99 million in September, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) announced Thursday. Despite last month’s improvement, the housing market remains fairly fragile, as existing-home sales are down 2.2% compared to last year.
